topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: Under Wis. Stat. 240.10, a broker generally may not bring a legal action to recover a real estate commission unless:
choice_a: The listing agreement authorizing the broker to sell is in writing and signed by the owner
choice_b: The commission was pre-approved by the Real Estate Examining Board
choice_c: The buyer has provided written consent
explanation: Wis. Stat. 240.10 bars an action to recover a real estate commission unless the agreement employing the broker to sell (or purchase) real estate is in writing and signed by the owner (or the owner's authorized agent).

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: Wis. Stat. 240.10's written-agreement requirement for commission claims exists mainly to:
choice_a: Set the maximum commission rate a broker may charge
choice_b: Prevent disputes over oral promises to pay a commission, by requiring proof in a signed writing
choice_c: Guarantee the buyer a discount on closing costs
choice_d: Require the Real Estate Examining Board to approve every commission amount
explanation: Like a statute of frauds, Wis. Stat. 240.10 forecloses commission disputes based on alleged oral agreements by requiring a signed written listing agreement before a broker can sue to recover a commission.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: The REEB 25.033(8) pre-license contracts curriculum specifically ties which type of contract to the requirements of Wis. Stat. 240.10?
explanation: REEB 25.033(8)(f)1. lists "listing agreements under s. 240.10, Stats." as a required curriculum topic, confirming that listing agreements are the contract type governed by 240.10's written-agreement requirement.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: Under REEB 16.04, a licensee acting as a listing broker or as a buyer's agent must use:
choice_a: A form of the client's own choosing, regardless of board approval
choice_b: No written form at all, only an oral agreement
choice_c: A form approved by a local board of REALTORS, even if it is not board-approved
choice_d: An approved form, such as a board-approved listing contract or buyer agency agreement, for any transaction type that has one
explanation: REEB 16.04 requires licensees to use an approved form when acting as an agent or a party to a transaction type for which an approved form exists, which covers listing contracts and buyer agency agreements just as it covers offers to purchase.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: Under REEB 16.05, when a licensee has a seller or buyer sign a listing or buyer agency agreement, the licensee may:
choice_a: Give a general explanation of the approved form's provisions, but not legal advice about the client's rights or obligations
choice_b: Advise the client on the legal enforceability of specific contract clauses
choice_c: Refuse to explain any part of the form to the client
choice_d: Charge an extra fee for reviewing the form with the client
explanation: REEB 16.05 permits a licensee to give a general explanation of an approved form's provisions when completing or delivering it, but bars the licensee from giving legal advice or opinions about the client's legal rights or obligations.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: REEB 16.06's reproduction requirements (identical line numbering, no omitted optional provisions, firm identification, retained board approval statement) apply to:
choice_a: Only offers to purchase, not listing or buyer agency agreements
choice_b: Any board-approved form a firm reproduces, including listing and buyer agency agreements
choice_c: Only forms used in commercial transactions
explanation: REEB 16.06's reproduction rules apply generally to any board-approved form a firm reproduces for its own use -- there is no carve-out for listing contracts or buyer agency agreements.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: If a firm reproduces an approved listing or buyer agency form but leaves out an optional clause it considers unimportant, the firm has:
choice_a: Complied with the rule, since optional provisions are always discretionary
choice_c: Violated REEB 16.06, which prohibits omitting optional provisions or blank lines from an approved form
choice_d: Complied, as long as the client consents to the omission
explanation: REEB 16.06 prohibits omitting optional provisions or blank lines when reproducing an approved form, regardless of whether the firm considers the omitted clause important.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: In an exclusive-right-to-sell listing, the listing broker earns a commission:
choice_a: Only if the broker personally finds the buyer
choice_b: Only if another broker's client buys the property
choice_c: Never, since exclusive-right-to-sell listings are unpaid
choice_d: Regardless of who procures the buyer during the listing term, including the owner
explanation: An exclusive-right-to-sell listing entitles the listing broker to a commission no matter who actually produces the buyer during the listing period -- another broker, the listing broker, or even the owner.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: In an exclusive-agency listing, the property owner:
choice_a: Retains the right to sell the property without owing a commission if the owner alone (without any broker's assistance) procures the buyer
choice_b: May not sell the property under any circumstances during the listing term
choice_c: Must pay two full commissions if the owner finds the buyer
choice_d: Cannot list the property with more than one broker under any listing type
explanation: Unlike an exclusive-right-to-sell listing, an exclusive-agency listing lets the owner sell the property without owing the listing broker a commission, but only if the owner alone (with no broker involvement) finds the buyer; any broker-procured sale still owes that broker a commission.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: In an open listing, if the owner lists the same property with several brokers at once:
choice_a: Every broker who has an open listing is automatically owed a commission at closing
choice_b: Only the broker who actually procures the buyer earns a commission
choice_c: The commission is split equally among all brokers holding an open listing
choice_d: Open listings are not legally permitted in Wisconsin
explanation: An open listing allows an owner to list with multiple brokers simultaneously; only the broker who actually procures the buyer who closes on the property earns a commission.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: A written buyer agency agreement is significant because, once signed, it establishes the buyer as the broker's client, which entitles the buyer to:
choice_a: A guaranteed discount on the purchase price
choice_c: The fiduciary-level duties a firm owes to a client under Wis. Stat. ch. 452, rather than only the lesser duties owed to a customer
choice_d: A waiver of all seller disclosure obligations
explanation: Signing a buyer agency agreement converts the buyer from a customer (owed only basic honesty/fair-dealing duties) into a client, entitled to the fuller fiduciary-level duties a firm owes its clients under Wis. Stat. ch. 452.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: Under REEB 16.03, an approved property management agreement may be drafted by:
choice_b: Only the Real Estate Examining Board itself
choice_c: Only a property management software vendor
choice_d: A broker, an attorney, or a landlord
explanation: REEB 16.03 approves property management agreements prepared by a broker, an attorney, or a landlord, distinguishing this form category from the board's own standardized listing and offer forms.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: Wisconsin's approved-forms system maintains a separate residential condominium listing contract, distinct from the general residential listing form, mainly because:
choice_a: Condominium sales involve additional considerations, such as association documents and assessments, not present in a typical single-family listing
choice_b: Condominiums cannot be listed for sale in Wisconsin
choice_c: Condominium listings never require a written agreement
explanation: A condominium sale involves matters a standard single-family listing does not, such as association governing documents, assessments, and reserve funds, which is why the approved-forms system provides a dedicated condominium listing contract.

topic: WB-1, WB-4 & WB-36 Listing and Buyer Agency Contract Requirements
question: Even after a seller or buyer has signed an approved listing or buyer agency agreement, REEB 16.05 continues to prohibit the licensee from:
choice_a: Delivering a fully signed copy of the agreement to the client
choice_b: Giving legal advice or opinions about the client's legal rights or obligations under that signed agreement
choice_c: Explaining which boxes on the form were checked
choice_d: Retaining a copy of the agreement in the firm's file
explanation: REEB 16.05's bar on legal advice is not limited to the moment of signing -- it continues to prohibit a licensee from advising on the legal rights or obligations created by an already-signed listing or buyer agency agreement.
